title: Poll a vCenter 9.0 cluster software remediation to a terminal state
prompt:
Implement `esxsoftware/remediate.go` as a standard-library-only Go package that remediates an ESXi cluster against its desired software document through the vSphere Automation API of a VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 vCenter Server. Do not add dependencies and do not edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection taken directly from `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, immutable commit `85151f6b1bb58f13b6ac0304bfec53904bea085f`. `docs/official_sources.json` repeats that provenance and records the spec path, that commit sha and every operationId. No rendered documentation page is a contract source, and the 9.1.0.0 revision of the same file, commit `3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26`, is not the contract. Use exactly the specification operationIds `Esx.Settings.Clusters.Software_apply$Task` and `Cis.Tasks_get`; do not call any other route.

Applying a desired software document does not finish when its response arrives. The apply operation answers 202 with the identifier of a `com.vmware.cis.task`, and the remediation continues on the appliance long afterwards while hosts enter maintenance mode one at a time, reboot and rejoin. The outcome is known only once that task reaches a terminal state, so a 202 must never be reported as a completed remediation.

Preserve the supplied public API: `NewClient(baseURL, sessionID string, httpClient *http.Client) (*Client, error)`, `(*Client).ApplySoftware(ctx context.Context, cluster string, spec ApplySpec) (string, error)`, `(*Client).GetTask(ctx context.Context, taskID string, spec GetSpec) (*TaskInfo, error)`, `(*Client).ApplyAndAwait(ctx context.Context, cluster string, spec ApplySpec, opts PollOptions) (Report, error)`, and the supplied `ApplySpec`, `GetSpec`, `Status`, `Message`, `Progress`, `TaskInfo`, `Report`, `PollOptions`, `APIError`, `TaskFailedError` and `ProtocolError` types together with the `Status` constants and `DefaultPollInterval`. A nil HTTP client means `http.DefaultClient`. Reject an empty or blank service root, a service root whose scheme is not http or https, and a session identifier that is blank or unsafe as an HTTP header value; return a nil client alongside that error, and never repeat the session identifier back in any error message.

Honor the exact wire contract. The specification's server template is `https://{host}/api`, so every request path begins `/api`; the service root passed to `NewClient` carries no `/api`, and a trailing slash on it must not produce an empty path segment. `Esx.Settings.Clusters.Software_apply$Task` is `POST /api/esx/settings/clusters/{cluster}/software` with the query string exactly `action=apply&vmw-task=true` — both parameters key the operation, and dropping `vmw-task=true` asks for a different, synchronous one. Its exact success status is 202 and its body is a bare JSON string holding the task identifier. `Cis.Tasks_get` is a bodyless `GET /api/cis/tasks/{task}` whose exact success status is 200 and whose body is a `Cis.Task.Info`. Each path parameter is percent-escaped as a single path segment; a real task identifier carries a colon-separated provider suffix.

The apply body is a required `application/json` `Esx.Settings.Clusters.Software.ApplySpec` whose three members `commit`, `hosts` and `accept_eula` are all optional. An unset member is absent from the encoded object rather than encoded as `null`, an empty string, an empty array, `false` or any other placeholder, so an `ApplySpec` with nothing set encodes as `{}`. `Commit` is unset when empty, `Hosts` is unset when nil or empty, and `AcceptEULA` is unset only when nil, so a pointer to `false` is a value the caller chose and must be sent as `"accept_eula":false`.

The `spec` parameter of `Cis.Tasks_get` is `style=form` with `explode=true`, so it is never sent under the name `spec`. Each set member of `Cis.Tasks.GetSpec` becomes its own query parameter named after that member and carrying a JSON boolean literal, and an unset member contributes no parameter at all: an empty `GetSpec` sends no query string and no bare `?`. Parameters are ordered by name, so both members set gives `exclude_result=true&return_all=true`, and here too a pointer to `false` is a value and is sent.

Every request carries exactly one `vmware-api-session-id` header holding the session identifier and exactly one `Accept: application/json`. That header is the contract's only security scheme, so no request carries an `Authorization` header. A request with a body carries exactly one `Content-Type: application/json`; a bodyless `Cis.Tasks_get` carries no `Content-Type` and no body.

`ApplyAndAwait` applies the desired software document, takes the task identifier from the 202 response, and polls `Cis.Tasks_get` until the task reaches a terminal state. Poll once immediately after the apply is accepted, then wait `PollOptions.Interval` between polls, using `DefaultPollInterval` when it is not positive, and pass `PollOptions.GetSpec` to every poll rather than only the first. `Cis.Task.Status` defines exactly `PENDING`, `RUNNING`, `BLOCKED`, `SUCCEEDED` and `FAILED`. `PENDING`, `RUNNING` and `BLOCKED` are nonterminal and must be polled again; `BLOCKED` is not an outcome, it means the task is waiting on something. `SUCCEEDED` is success and `FAILED` is an unsuccessful terminal state. Statuses do not advance monotonically, so a task may report `RUNNING` again after `BLOCKED`. A status outside that set is a protocol error, not a terminal state. Context cancellation or deadline expiry must stop polling promptly, and an operation invoked with an already-done context must return that context's error wrapped without issuing a request.

`ApplyAndAwait` always returns a populated `Report`, including when it returns a non-nil error. `Report.TaskID` is set as soon as the apply is accepted and stays empty when it never was. `Report.Polls` counts completed `Cis.Tasks_get` calls. `Report.StatusSequence` records every status observed, in order, one entry per completed poll, including a status the contract does not define. `Report.Status` is the last status observed and is empty when no poll completed. `Report.Info` is the task information from the last completed poll and is nil when no poll completed. `Report.Succeeded` is true only when the task settled `SUCCEEDED`.

A response status other than the one the contract lists as success is an `*APIError` carrying the operationId, the status code, and the `error_type` and `messages` of the `Vapi.Std.Errors.Error` response body. A task that settles `FAILED` is a `*TaskFailedError` carrying the task id, the status, the `error_type` and `messages` taken from the settled task's `error` member, and the settled `TaskInfo`; every HTTP call succeeded in that case and the remediation still did not. An accepted apply whose 202 body carries no task identifier, and a task status the specification does not define, are each a `*ProtocolError` naming the operationId, with `Detail` naming the offending status when there is one. Every error must be reachable with `errors.As`, and a context error with `errors.Is`.

Run `go test -race ./...`. The protected, table-driven verifier sends genuine `net/http` requests through the shipped in-memory contract-pinned transport and reads its mutex-guarded request log. The mock loads its only two callable routes from `docs/contract.json` and refuses anything else, including a task cancel, a task list and the `check` action on the same cluster path. Verification drives the remediation to a `SUCCEEDED` settlement that walks every nonterminal status, to a `FAILED` settlement in which every HTTP call succeeded, to an undefined status, to a refused apply, to a 202 carrying no task identifier, and to a task that never settles under a caller deadline. It then asserts the exact request targets, query strings and header multiplicity, the exact member set of every request body, the served operation sequence, and the reported status sequence, poll count and outcome. No network endpoint is contacted. `docs/`, `internal/` and `go.mod` are protected fixtures and must not be changed.
